p.src: When I was young, I knew a man named Jin Guang. After I failed the college entrance exam the first time, I spent another year preparing, and finally entered a university I did not like. Around the end of my first year, during a summer visit home, I met Jin Guang on a bright afternoon. He had already become a contractor in the early wave of real estate fever.

Around the end of my first year, during a summer visit home, I met Jin Guang on a bright afternoon. He had already become a contractor in the early wave of real estate fever.

p.src: It was 1992. China was changing fast. People who sensed the shift were borrowing money, starting businesses, chasing projects, and stepping into risks they did not fully understand. Contractors looked especially impressive. Jin Guang was short, wore jeans, had a close haircut, and carried one of those large early mobile phones that looked glamorous at the time and absurd later.

p.src: We walked to the river and sat on the embankment for an afternoon.

u.src: We walked to the river and sat on the embankment for an afternoon.

p.src: I knew his situation was not easy. He had borrowed heavily. He was young. He lacked experience. Money was trapped in projects. Older and sharper people had surrounded him. There were delays, debts, traps, and pressures.

u.src: I knew his situation was not easy. He had borrowed heavily. He was young. He lacked experience. Money was trapped in projects. Older and sharper people had surrounded him. There were delays, debts, traps, and pressures.

p.src: Yet all afternoon he talked about interesting things. He laughed. He told stories. He did not mention his hardship. Not once.

u.src: Yet all afternoon he talked about interesting things. He laughed. He told stories. He did not mention his hardship. Not once.
en: Yet all afternoon he talked about interesting things. He laughed. He told stories. He did not mention his hardship. Not once.

p.src: At first I thought of asking about his troubles, but I quickly saw the uselessness of my concern. I had no ability to solve his problems. My sympathy would have been only a performance. Perhaps he was proud. Perhaps he simply had a better instinct. Whatever the reason, his refusal to complain entered me deeply.

p.src: Many years later, I met him again by accident on a train to Shenyang. By then I had graduated, worked for two years, and was preparing to study abroad. Jin Guang had not become the successful contractor people imagined. He had debts and years of trouble behind him. He was on his way to Russia to find a new path.

p.src: But when I saw him, it felt as if no time had passed. Same smile, same brightness, same easy manner. The large phone had become a thinner Nokia. The rest was unchanged. We talked through the night. Again, there was no complaint. No bitterness. No list of people who had wronged him. No display of suffering.

p.src: Some friends comfort you when you complain. Such friends may be kind, and kindness should be valued. p.src: Why does he get credit?

u.src: Why does he get credit?
en: Why does he get credit?

p.src: Why am I treated this way?

u.src: Why am I treated this way?
en: Why am I treated this way?

p.src: Sometimes these complaints point to real problems. Credit matters. Fairness matters. Negotiation matters. A person should not romanticize being ignored.

u.src: Sometimes these complaints point to real problems. Credit matters. Fairness matters. Negotiation matters. A person should not romanticize being ignored.

p.src: But recognition is dangerous when treated as oxygen. If you cannot act without applause, then other people own your emotional engine. Better to treat recognition as an extra gift. Welcome it when it comes. Do not make it the condition for doing what is right, useful, or necessary.

p.src: This adjustment saves enormous attention. Instead of arguing endlessly about who is right, who noticed, who praised, and who failed to praise, you can return to the work itself.

u.src: This adjustment saves enormous attention. Instead of arguing endlessly about who is right, who noticed, who praised, and who failed to praise, you can return to the work itself.

p.src: Complaint tends to obsess over correctness. Freedom tends to ask for a way forward.

u.src: Complaint tends to obsess over correctness. Freedom tends to ask for a way forward.
en: Complaint tends to obsess over correctness. Freedom tends to ask for a way forward.

p.src: To remain tangled in right and wrong is to live tangled. To search for a way out is to live more freely.

u.src: To remain tangled in right and wrong is to live tangled. To search for a way out is to live more freely.
en: To remain tangled in right and wrong is to live tangled. To search for a way out is to live more freely.

p.src: The Real Target

u.src: The Real Target
en: The Real Target

p.src: When we complain about life, the hidden target is often ourselves.

u.src: When we complain about life, the hidden target is often ourselves.
en: When we complain about life, the hidden target is often ourselves.

p.src: We are dissatisfied with our weakness, but we describe it as dissatisfaction with the world. We are angry at our dependency, but we describe it as anger at other people. We are ashamed of our lack of options, but we describe it as proof that options do not exist.

u.src: We are dissatisfied with our weakness, but we describe it as dissatisfaction with the world. We are angry at our dependency, but we describe it as anger at other people. We are ashamed of our lack of options, but we describe it as proof that options do not exist.
en: We are dissatisfied with our weakness, but we describe it as dissatisfaction with the world. We are angry at our dependency, but we describe it as anger at other people. We are ashamed of our lack of options, but we describe it as proof that options do not exist.

p.src: This is why quitting complaint feels uncomfortable. It removes a shelter. Once the words stop, the remaining facts become visible.

u.src: This is why quitting complaint feels uncomfortable. It removes a shelter. Once the words stop, the remaining facts become visible.
en: This is why quitting complaint feels uncomfortable. It removes a shelter. Once the words stop, the remaining facts become visible.

p.src: But visibility is the beginning of power.

u.src: But visibility is the beginning of power.
en: But visibility is the beginning of power.

p.src: A person who stops complaining still has problems. He may still be poor, tired, wronged, behind, anxious, or unprepared. The difference is that his attention is no longer leaking through language. It can be gathered and spent.

u.src: A person who stops complaining still has problems. He may still be poor, tired, wronged, behind, anxious, or unprepared. The difference is that his attention is no longer leaking through language. It can be gathered and spent.

p.src: The practice is severe and small:

u.src: The practice is severe and small:
en: The practice is severe and small:

p.src: Stop saying the complaint aloud.

u.src: Stop saying the complaint aloud.
en: Stop saying the complaint aloud.

p.src: Record each failure without drama.

u.src: Record each failure without drama.
en: Record each failure without drama.

p.src: Identify the missing ability.

u.src: Identify the missing ability.
en: Identify the missing ability.

p.src: Improve what can be improved.

u.src: Improve what can be improved.
en: Improve what can be improved.

p.src: Endure what cannot yet be changed.

u.src: Endure what cannot yet be changed.
en: Endure what cannot yet be changed.

p.src: Distance yourself, where possible, from chronic complaint.

u.src: Distance yourself, where possible, from chronic complaint.
en: Distance yourself, where possible, from chronic complaint.

p.src: This is not positive thinking. It is resource protection.

u.src: This is not positive thinking. It is resource protection.
en: This is not positive thinking. It is resource protection.

p.src: The road to wealth freedom asks a person to become a better allocator: of money, time, effort, trust, risk, and attention. Complaint is bad allocation at the level of speech. It pays attention to pain without buying capacity. It spends emotion without purchasing clarity. It turns hardship into identity instead of material for growth.

p.src: Cherish life. Stay away from complaint, especially your own.
